$description: Three faces. Pixel Bop, Blip's own pixel font, for big text: always on the grid, always capitals. Pixel Operator for UI and body text, with Pixelify Sans for the letters it does not draw, because a 7-pixel font is too small to read at body sizes: drawn on a 16-pixel em, so at the 16 px body size each of its pixels is a CSS pixel, finer than the grid.

display.$description: Pixel Bop, in Latin, Cyrillic and Greek. Sized in whole scales: 1 em is 10 pixels, caps are 7 pixels tall. Then Pixelify Sans, emoji sized to the capitals (Blip Fallback, in @jaatster/blip-font) and the system font for other scripts.

ui.$description: Pixel Operator, regular and bold, in Latin. Its grid is 16 pixels to the em, so it is sharpest at 16 and 32 px. Then Pixelify Sans for what it does not draw (Cyrillic, Greek, most of Latin Extended), emoji sized to the capitals (Blip Fallback, in @jaatster/blip-font) and the system font for other scripts.

display-scale.$description: Pixel Bop sizes, as whole scales of the pixel. Font size = 10 x pixel x scale; cap height = 7 x pixel x scale.

size.$description: UI and body text sizes, in rem: 12, 14, 16, 18 and 22 px at the browser's default text size (16 px), and larger when the person sets a larger default. Not tied to the pixel size, so text stays readable when the pixel grows.

display-loose.$description: Stacked display lines with accented capitals.
